newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat down on European weather, U.S. crops.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat down on European weather, U.S. crops.

text.p: Improvement in the condition of the U.S. wheat crop and drought-relieving rains in Europe pushed CBOT wheat futures lower at midsession, floor traders said.
"Everybody is focusing on the improvement in crop conditions for the wheat," said one CBOT floor trader.
On Monday in its weekly crop progress reports, the U.S. Department of Agriculture showed modest improvement in the hard red winter wheat crops in Kansas, Texas and Oklahoma.
Early reports from a wheat crop tour sponsored by the Wheat Quality Council also supported the USDA data.

In Kansas, wheat frozen by a spring frost was showing signs of development. Some crops thought to be damaged by the cold were putting out tillers, which later develop into heads and produce grain, crop tour participants said.
Tuesday's forecasts for rain in drought-stricken areas of Europe also weighed on wheat prices, traders said.
In early trade, Smith Barney sold two milliion bushels July, pit sources said. Rand Financial, Refco and Prudential Securities were also noted sellers, sources said.
At 1103 CDT, wheat was down 8-1/2 to two cents per bushel, with July down 6-1/4 at $4.05 per bushel.
